_comment: Pre-registered probes for the 4.0.1 consolidation (SEC-3 served model, SEC-8 spec-axis catch rate) and the ordinary-work negative that replaces the staff-engineer must_not_dispatch. NOTHING HAS BEEN RUN. This file is pinned by FREEZE.sha256 and committed before any model run: a threshold changed after a run is a new, disclosed revision and never rescues that run. Scorer: check-probes.py (reads only this file).

registered.revision: pre-run re-pin (review N1, N2, N3, N5, S-9; user decision U30): E20 is scored from a closed form only. The reviewer prompt (eval/prompts/E20-spec-axis-seeded-violations.md) requires one `AC-n: MET` or `AC-n: VIOLATED` line per criterion; check-probes.py reads ONLY lines of that form (verdict_line_regex) and no natural-language heuristic; a run with a criterion lacking such a line, a duplicate or conflicting line, or no such line at all is UNSCORABLE (exit 2) for human adjudication; a trace count other than `runs` is UNSCORABLE. The heuristic fields of the first pre-run re-pin (violation_word_regex, weak_violation_regex, negated_violation_regex, cleared_word_regex) are removed. Thresholds unchanged. No model has run, so this is not a post-run change. Second pre-run re-pin (iter 5, review F1; user decision U30): the verdict lines are read ONLY from the tool_result of the spec reviewer's own spawn; the router's final text can only corroborate (conflict = UNSCORABLE) and never supplies a missing line; the E19 and E20 prompt files are now pinned in this set's FREEZE.sha256.
registered.what_a_run_is: one fresh `claude -p` session of the router on the fixture of the scenario (scripts/eval-fixture-core.sh --scenario <id>), same model tier as the 4.0.0 routing baseline (Sonnet), stream-json trace kept

E19.claim: an upward per-invocation model override is passed on the dispatch and the requested and the served model are both recorded; a mismatch is BLOCKED, never PASS
E19.pass_rule: 5 of 5 runs record the override dispatch and both models correctly, and 5 of 5 are served as requested (modelUsage names the requested family): the control is a binary host-pinning substitute, one miss is a failed control
E19.unscorable_when: the result event carries no modelUsage (the served model cannot be checked) or the number of traces given is not exactly `runs`

E20.claim: the spec-axis reviewer (a fresh plan spawn that never wrote the AC) reports the acceptance-criteria violations seeded in a change whose unit tests are green

seeded_violations.AC-2: rows ordered descending, spec says ascending
seeded_violations.AC-3: no quoting of comma or double quote
seeded_violations.AC-4: empty log raises instead of returning the header

E20.verdict_rule: structured text scorer with human adjudication. The scorer reads only lines whose whole stripped text is `AC-n: MET` or `AC-n: VIOLATED` (upper case, one space after the colon, nothing else on the line); it reads no other wording. A catch is a seeded id with VIOLATED; a false positive is a decoy id with VIOLATED. Two lines for one id in one reply, the same id with two different verdicts, a criterion without a line, or no line at all makes the run UNSCORABLE (exit 2): a human reads the reply and decides. The lines are taken ONLY from the spec reviewer's own spawn result (the tool_result of its `plan` spawn); the router's final text may only corroborate them: a different verdict there is a conflict (UNSCORABLE), and a line missing from the reviewer's reply is UNSCORABLE even when the final text has it (a prose-only or partial reviewer is never completed by the router).

threshold.rates_over: all runs: caught / (runs x 4 seeded), flagged decoys / (runs x 2 decoys)

E20.baseline: the same 5 runs on the 4.0.0 tree (business-analyst as the spec reviewer), same checker with --spec-agent business-analyst; its catch rate is passed to the 4.0.1 verdict with --baseline-rate. No baseline = only the absolute threshold applies, and the report says so.
E20.unscorable_when: the number of traces given is not exactly `runs`, or any run lacks, in the spec reviewer's own spawn result, a closed-form `AC-n: MET|VIOLATED` line for a criterion (or has none, a duplicate, a conflicting one, or no spec-reviewer reply at all)

ordinary_work_negative.replaces: staff-engineer in expected.must_not_dispatch of the ordinary-work scenarios (E01, E07, E11, E12, E15), dropped by the 4.0.1 derivation because the staff-grade brief is now a `build` mode
ordinary_work_negative.rule: no main-session spawn carries a fable model request and the result's modelUsage names no fable model: ordinary work must not be over-dispatched to the staff-grade tier
ordinary_work_negative.unscorable_when: never; a trace without modelUsage is checked on the dispatch requests only and the report says so

fallback.trigger: E20 fails its pre-registered threshold on the 4.0.1 runs (or is below the 4.0.0 baseline), or the measured catch rate cannot be shown to be equal to the baseline within the registered rule
fallback.action: the spec axis moves from `plan` to `verify` (a spec mode of the verify type, a fresh spawn that never wrote the AC): the router review card, plan.md, verify.md and the tool ceiling test change in the same revision; plan keeps requirements, architecture and domain
fallback.e19_trigger: E19 fails (any of the 5 runs): the per-dispatch model override is not honoured or not recorded; domain, architecture and staff-grade briefs then run at the type default and the router reports BLOCKED for them until the user decides between a host-pinned domain type and an accepted lower tier
fallback.decision_owner: the user; no agent applies the fallback by itself
